subject: religious-studies
title: Prayer Across the Faiths
welcome_lead: Discover how believers around the world talk to the divine through prayer.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on prayer practices across world religions.
final_note: You've learned how prayer takes many forms across the world's religions.

concepts.def: Communication with God or the divine.
Five daily Islamic prayers facing Mecca.
Famous Christian prayer taught by Jesus.
Key Jewish prayer declaring belief in one God.
Sacred sound or phrase repeated in Hindu prayer.
Quiet focus to calm and train the mind.

walkthroughs.body_html: Muslims perform Salah five times a day facing Mecca. Many Christians pray daily, often using the Lord's Prayer. Jews recite the Shema morning and evening. Hindus may chant mantras at home shrines.

Prayer can involve standing, kneeling, bowing or sitting. Muslims use prayer mats; Christians may kneel; Buddhists often sit cross-legged in meditation. People pray in places of worship, at home and even at school or work.
Prayer can be praise, thanks, asking for help, confession, or simply quiet reflection. It helps believers feel close to God and part of a community of faith.
